title: Introduce sandboxed RAG plugin hot-reload playground and devcontainer quickstart
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a local-first RAG playground with hot-reloadable tool/plugin stubs, a devcontainer for onboarding, and updated docs + quickstart. No breaking API changes. Recommended for developer experience and authoring demos.
description:
Motivation: Developer onboarding for RAG-based agents often requires multiple moving parts (indexers, plugin/tool stubs, agent runtime). This PR introduces a local sandboxed playground that bundles a tiny indexer, a hot-reloadable plugin shim, TypeScript and Python agent examples, and a VS Code devcontainer that lets engineers iterate on tool implementations without restarting the agent process. The goal is to reduce the feedback loop for plugin/tool development and make it trivial to reproduce dev-friendly scenarios for demos and workshops.

What this PR does (summary):
- New example: examples/sandboxed-rag-playground - a self-contained playground that runs a small vector indexer (local SQLite+FAISS stub), a Redwood-compatible agent shim, and a hot-reload plugin process that communicates over a WebSocket control plane.
- Hot-reload: plugin-shim.ts implements a file-watch + module reloader for local TS plugins. Python agents can load plugins dynamically via a thin HTTP bridge. Changes to plugin files are picked up within ~200ms in the playground, enabling live iteration.
- Devcontainer: .devcontainer provides a reproducible dev environment (Node 20, Python 3.11, Poetry, Rust toolchain for compiling local indexer bindings) so engineers can 'Open in Dev Container' and follow the quickstart.
- Quickstart docs: docs/quickstarts/sandboxed-rag-hotreload.md walks through running the playground, connecting the Redwood API key, and authoring a simple tool that performs entity extraction + structured output.
- Telemetry: adds a minimal telemetry probe config (telemetry/probes.yaml) for capturing token-level latency and plugin call counts in the playground. This is intentionally opt-in and local-only.

Checklist: [x] playground scaffolded [x] TS + Python agent examples [x] devcontainer + docker-compose [x] quickstart docs [x] basic telemetry probes [x] CI smoke workflow for quickstart boot [ ] add workshop exercises (follow-up)

Commits (high level):
- Initial scaffold: playground folder, devcontainer, README
- Add TS agent example and hot-reload plugin shim
- Add Python agent example and local indexer script
- Add telemetry probes and quickstart docs
- CI: smoke workflow to bring up minimal services and run basic end-to-end smoke test

Files changed (high level):
- README.md: new top-level quickstart instructions + troubleshooting notes for macOS/WSL
- devcontainer files: reproducible env for new engineers, includes VS Code forwarding for ports and host networking hints
- ts-agent/index.ts: compact agent example showing structured outputs, function/tool calling and usage of Redwood SDK client with streaming compatibility.
- hotreload/plugin-shim.ts: file-watcher + in-memory reload with graceful fallback to previous implementation on runtime errors.
- py_agent/agent.py: Python equivalent demonstrating plugin bridge via HTTP endpoints and local indexer integration.
- indexer/local_indexer.py: tiny indexer using SQLite for persistence with an in-memory embedding fallback for offline-first demos.
- docs/quickstarts/sandboxed-rag-hotreload.md: step-by-step quickstart, sample prompts, and troubleshooting section.
- .github/workflows/smoke-ci.yml: lightweight CI that builds the devcontainer and runs the playground compose stack, then executes a scripted agent request to assert end-to-end flow.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Arjun Patel: "Love the devcontainer approach. Two asks: (1) Can the hot-reload fallback be more explicit in logs when a plugin fails to compile? (2) Add a note about not using this as a production pattern."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added explicit fallback logs and a 'local-only' warning in README. Also added defensive try/catch and a health endpoint for the plugin shim so CI can detect plugin failure quickly."
- Samantha Lee: "The telemetry probes look fine but please make them opt-in by default."
- Maya Chen: "Telemetry is disabled by default; quickstart shows how to enable local probes. Updated docs to call this out."
- Rocio Morales: "Please ensure the quickstart includes steps to connect a hosted Redwood API key and the expected environment variables."
- Maya Chen: "Added environment variable section, sample .env.example, and a credential safety note."

CI and merge: CI passed on the final push after adding fallback logs. A lightweight smoke CI created by the workflow verified the compose stack and executed a validated agent request. No flakiness observed during runs. PR was squash-merged to main on 2026-02-24 after approvals from Arjun and Samantha. Merge method: squash.

Follow-ups planned:
- ENG-1420-1: convert local indexer to use a small Go binary for improved perf in workshop settings.
- DES-89-2: author two workshop exercises for the docs site with assertions and sample datasets.
- Optional: integrate the playground with the playground catalog so it shows up on the examples index (implementation dependent).

Notes for maintainers: keep the playground lightweight and explicitly marked as a developer-first tool. Do not add production model keys or credentials. The telemetry probes are local-only and opt-in. If we extend this playground for workshops, we should add versioned datasets and a deterministic seeding mechanism for reproducible demos.
